invariant: At most one pending invitation per mailbox. InvitationId and generation live in state and every release compares both; generation is never part of the stream key.
mustPreserve: Retry same invitation ID with exact terms returns original acceptance; changed terms conflict. New invitation generation is independent. Delivery retries preserve exact token and accepted at-least-once policy.
identityReadingRule: selectedIdentitySummary and exact selectedCommandContracts define intended identity. baselineIdentityObservation/declaredIdentity retain older source observations only, including old replay defects; they are not target behavior or authorization to change an occupied key.

logicalIdentity.rule: caller-supplied immutable creation identity: an exact retry with the same id and authored intent returns the original result; the same id with changed intent is refused; a different id is a different record

identityContractRule: Existing published owner identity/IdFor remains stable. Required typed creation/operation identity and tenant/program/source scope come from the selected signature/protocol references; no context.RequestId minting fallback or guessed new stream key.
selectedIdentitySummary: Tenant-scoped tenant / normalizedEmail; `TenantInvitationIds.AcceptanceOf(InvitationId)` on `AcceptTenantInvitation` is the caller-supplied immutable creation identity (recorded from source 2026-10-29) so an exact retry resolves the original result and a different id is a different record; later mutations use CommandId bound to this identity and the expected revision.
selectedReplayRule: Current required authorization precedes replay; exact authorized retries resolve the original accepted result using the selected logical identity and immutable actor/intent/source binding. Fresh mutable feasibility, clock selection and body preparation cannot replace that original result. Expected revision is concurrency precondition, not a new identity.
commandNote: No standalone command. The mailbox owner is claimed inline (TenantInvitationMailboxes.AcquireAsync, supersedes an unusable holder) by the three invite handlers before the invitation fact, and released inline (ReleaseAsync with exact holder+generation, else no-op) by AcceptTenantInvitation. Treat as service-called side effects of those commands, not independent commands.
